newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE says 132,044 illegal aliens have left.
newsitem.headline: UAE says 132,044 illegal aliens have left.

text.p: More than 130,000 illegal workers have left the United Arab Emirates ahead of a new law cracking down on unlawful foreign labour, an interior ministry official was on Thursday quoted as saying.

Interior Ministry undersecretary Major General Saqer Ghabash told al-Ittihad newspaper that 132,044 illegal workers had left the UAE by September 30, the day a two-month government amnesty for illegal workers to leave or legalise their stay expired.
The government has since extended the amnesty to the end of October as many workers said they needed more time to organise departures and airlines said they could not cope with the rush.
The UAE has estimated that some 140,000 illegal aliens will depart during the three-month amnesty. Diplomats say as many as 200,000 could leave by the end of October.
"Statistics showed that 12,371 illegal workers left on one day which is September 30," said Ghabash, who added that the new amnesty would not be extended further.
He said the new law will help curb crime "as statistics showed that a high percentage of criminals are illegal workers".
The government has said illegal aliens are a threat to the UAE's security.

Thousands of foreign workers -- primarily from the Indian subcontinent but also from southeast Asia -- have been rushing to leave the UAE by plane and ship to avoid tough penalties when the new law takes effect on November 1.
If they are caught after the deadline, they face punishments including fines, prison terms and deportation.

A passenger ship carrying 1,521 workers left for Bombay on Wednesday after a 30-hour delay due to technical problems, newspapers said. They said the ship, al-Madina, was due to arrive in Bombay on October 7. A cargo ship carrying 1,300 illegal aliens left on Monday.

Foreigners make up about 75 percent of the 2.4 million population in the small Gulf state. Many came to the Gulf legally, but broke the law by failing to leave when their visas expired or working for employers other than their sponsors.
Ghabash said those who have left would be allowed to return to the UAE if they obtain the legal documents.

He said the UAE "appreciates the role of foreign workers in different development projects and opens its doors to any person arriving to work in the country legally even if they were the illegal workers who left the country and wish to come back in a legal way."
